groups.title: Nominal-embed foundation and object valence
groups.proposal: Build incorporation as one integrated compound operation that combines an owner-issued NNC Result with an owner-issued VNC Result. Preserve the complete typed Sources, derive the NNC's general-use nounstem shape, and classify the grammatical relation as incorporated object, incorporated adverb, or incorporated complement. For incorporated objects, consume exactly one object-valence position and keep the embedded nounstem distinct from any remaining nuclear object.
groups.writingJob: Combine open typed NNC and VNC Results inside one boundaried Source, derive ordinary general-use nounstem shape including the regular retained-a condition, preserve genuinely lexical exceptional shape only when typed, and reduce a transitive matrix by exactly one object-valence level when the embed is an incorporated object.
groups.readingJob: Show the NNC and VNC source boundaries, general-use nounstem, the three incorporation relations, incorporated-versus-nuclear object contrast, exact valence change, retained-a evidence, lexical exceptions, and Canvas examples as proof rather than admission lists.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses Incorporation, the owner-issued NNC and VNC Results, and the intended incorporation relation when the Source leaves more than one real analysis open. The application derives nounstem shape, boundaries, compatibility, valence effects, and cues.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse canonical Result capture and a conditional Analysis choice; do not add witness-stem pickers, noun or verb whitelists, manual boundary controls, manual retained-a controls, or a valence-reduction switch.

groups.title: Single-object incorporation
groups.proposal: For an incorporated object inside a single-object transitive matrix, let the nominal embed fill that object position and derive an intransitive compound. Suppress object pronouns automatically, preserve the finite subject, and keep every compatible typed NNC and VNC Source open. Treat special lexical shapes and meanings as typed exceptions or reading facts, never as route authorization.
groups.writingJob: Insert the selected general-use nounstem into a single-object matrix, consume its sole object-valence position, derive an intransitive Result with no object carrier, preserve subject and Source-shape evidence, and allow ordinary later derivation from the canonical Result.
groups.readingJob: Show the incorporated patient area, intransitive output, absent object pronoun, retained finite subject, source boundaries, normal and exceptional nounstem shapes, later-derivation availability, and examples as evidence.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the NNC Result and compatible single-object VNC Result. The application derives incorporation, object satisfaction, intransitivity, participant carriers, form, and continuation; lexical readings do not become controls.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Source, Result capture, and Later derivation; do not add object-pronoun, valence, example, gloss, stem-membership, or special-water-form controls.

groups.title: Higher-valence object incorporation
groups.proposal: Apply the same productive operation to double- and triple-object matrices. Incorporation consumes one correctly typed object level, producing respectively a single-object or double-object compound while preserving all other participants and shuntline relations. Any later causative or applicative operates on the complete canonical Result through the shared continuation path.
groups.writingJob: Match the nominal embed to the typed object role it satisfies, lower matrix valence by one, preserve every remaining subject and object carrier in its proper relation, retain internal Source boundaries, and pass the completed Result unchanged into later licensed derivations.
groups.readingJob: Show which object role was incorporated, which participants remain nuclear, the one-level valence reduction, silent or nonspecific object replacement, shuntline structure, nested derivational boundaries, and examples as evidence.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the NNC Result, higher-valence VNC Result, and the incorporated object role only when the typed Source permits more than one genuine match. The application derives all valence, carrier, boundary, and continuation consequences.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse typed participant roles and Later derivation; do not add manual valence, participant-copy, shuntline, derivation-depth, example, or stem-list controls.

groups.title: Exceptional tla fusion and Source ambiguity
groups.proposal: Preserve the exceptional construction in which a nominal embed combines with a tla-fused intransitive matrix and receives an adverbial form-or-nature reading. Keep it structurally distinct from ordinary means incorporation, and expose an Analysis choice only when the same typed surface genuinely permits both Source histories.
groups.writingJob: Build the exceptional nominal-plus-tla-fused Source only from the required typed analysis, preserve intransitive valence, derive its adverbial relation, and maintain distinct canonical analyses for genuinely ambiguous forms.
groups.readingJob: Show tla-fused matrix structure, intransitivity, form-or-nature reading, contrast with ordinary means incorporation, genuine ambiguity, and witness examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the exceptional Source analysis where intended and resolves Source history only when both analyses remain grammatically possible. All form and valence consequences are automatic.
groups.controlPolicy: Use a conditional Analysis choice; do not infer the exceptional route from surface spelling alone or authorize it from an example list.

groups.title: Incorporated-adverb foundation
groups.proposal: Treat incorporated adverbs as one relation with two possible Source histories: an ordinary adverbial NNC adjunct or a transformed supplementary participant. Preserve matrix valence, and keep the histories distinct even when they share a surface form.
groups.writingJob: Attach the typed nominal embed adverbially without consuming matrix valence, preserve all participants, record the correct Source history, and leave the Result open to later adverb-related operations.
groups.readingJob: Show adverbial relation, unchanged valence, the two Source histories, surface equivalence without analytical collapse, later-path availability, and examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the NNC and VNC Results and resolves Source history only when grammar does not already determine it. The application preserves valence and derives structure and cues.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse conditional Analysis and canonical continuation; do not create gloss, idiom, surface-form, or example controls.

groups.title: Means and instrument adverbs
groups.proposal: Derive means and instrument incorporation from the typed adverbial relation. Keep the nominal embed from becoming the subject, preserve matrix valence, and delete an intimate-possessor relation automatically only when its referent is already a matrix participant.
groups.writingJob: Incorporate a means or instrument nominal, preserve matrix participants and valence, derive coreferential intimate-possession deletion from referent identity, and preserve exceptional fusions only as typed Source analyses.
groups.readingJob: Show means or instrument role, non-subject status, possessor coreference and deletion, unchanged valence, source-boundary evidence, lexical fusions, and examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the nominal and matrix Results; a referent choice appears only where identity is genuinely unspecified. The application derives possession deletion, valence, and form.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse referent identity; do not add possessor-deletion, subject, valence, example, or fused-stem admission controls.

groups.title: Place adverbs
groups.proposal: Derive place incorporation through the same adverbial owner. Preserve matrix valence and participants, allow compound NNC embeds, and apply intimate-possession deletion only from typed coreference.
groups.writingJob: Incorporate a typed place-denoting NNC Result, preserve its internal shape and any compound boundaries, retain matrix valence, and derive possessor suppression when referent identity licenses it.
groups.readingJob: Show place relation, compound embed structure, participant continuity, valence preservation, possessor linkage or deletion, and examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the NNC and VNC Results and only unresolved referent identity. Place structure and its consequences are automatic.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse canonical capture and referent identity; do not add place-example, compound-template, possession, or valence controls.

groups.title: Time, duration, cause, and purpose adverbs
groups.proposal: Apply incorporated-adverb structure to time, duration, cause, and purpose relations while preserving matrix valence. Let typed grammar choose the relation when it can; request an Analysis only where the Source genuinely leaves multiple relations possible, and never let an English gloss authorize the route.
groups.writingJob: Attach the nominal embed with its typed temporal, durational, causal, or purposive relation, preserve participants and valence, and retain contextual readings including lack readings without turning them into lexical gates.
groups.readingJob: Show the adverb relation, temporal extent or causal scope, contextual purpose and lack readings, unchanged valence, source boundaries, and examples as evidence.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses an Analysis only when multiple grammatical relations remain possible. The application derives all structure, scope, participants, form, and compatible readings.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not add translation, meaning, example, valence, or stem-membership controls; reuse conditional Analysis.

groups.title: Manner and compared-manner adverbs
groups.proposal: Derive ordinary and compared-manner incorporation from typed adverb structure. Intransitive matrices make comparison subject-oriented; transitive matrices may leave a genuine subject-versus-object comparison choice. Preserve cause-versus-manner ambiguity only where both Source analyses remain possible.
groups.writingJob: Build manner or compared-manner embeds, preserve matrix valence, derive the comparison target from matrix structure when unique, and expose target or relation Analysis only for genuine transitive or Source-history ambiguity.
groups.readingJob: Show manner relation, form-or-style reading, compared participant, subject and object orientation, valence, cause-purpose contrast, genuine ambiguities, and examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the compared participant only where a transitive matrix permits both, and chooses cause versus compared manner only where Source evidence does not decide. All other orientation is automatic.
groups.controlPolicy: Use conditional Comparison target and Analysis choices; do not add translation, witness, automatic-subject, or automatic-object controls.

groups.title: Unique embed nounstems
groups.proposal: Preserve the small lexical inventory of unique incorporated nounstems as lexical Source analyses, not productive route authorization. Let their typed shape participate in the ordinary incorporation pipeline and preserve destockal, frequentative, and supportive-vowel distinctions through continuation.
groups.writingJob: Accept a typed unique embed analysis, combine it through the shared incorporation operation, preserve exact morphemic Source structure and vowel evidence, and allow ordinary licensed continuation without generalizing its lexical identity.
groups.readingJob: Show lexical embed identity, uncertain or historical meaning, Source reconstruction, real versus supportive i, destockal or frequentative shape, later boundaries, and Canvas evidence.
groups.decisionSplit: The user supplies a genuinely lexical embed analysis when it is not already known. The application derives all productive incorporation and continuation behavior from typed structure.
groups.controlPolicy: A lexical inventory may identify lexical facts but must never hide or block other grammatically valid incorporation Sources; do not create a productive route whitelist.

groups.title: Possessive supplementary-subject adverbs
groups.proposal: Transform a possessive supplementary subject of an intransitive principal into an incorporated adverb while promoting its possessor to the finite nominative subject. Preserve the semantic link between possessor and embedded noun, and keep supplementation and incorporation as distinct roles in one canonical derivation history.
groups.writingJob: Recapture the typed principal and possessive supplement, incorporate the possessed nominal adverbially, promote the possessor to matrix subject, preserve referent identity and unchanged matrix valence, and distinguish compared-manner analysis where genuinely ambiguous.
groups.readingJob: Show supplementary-source history, possessor-to-subject promotion, embedded body-part, clothing, or kin relation, referent link, adverb role, valence, compared-manner contrast, and examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The user selects the owner-issued principal and supplementary NNC and resolves supplementation-derived versus compared-manner analysis only where both remain possible. Promotion and referent linkage are automatic.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Lesson 17 capture and referent identity; do not add manual subject-copy, possessor-promotion, kin/body-part lists as route gates, or a second supplementation engine.

groups.title: Possessive supplementary-object and passive adverbs
groups.proposal: Transform a possessive supplementary object of a transitive principal into an incorporated adverb while promoting its possessor to the matrix object. Also allow an active supplementary subject to become an incorporated adverb when ordinary passive formation discards the active subject. Preserve intimate-possession restrictions and keep passive agents unmentionable.
groups.writingJob: Recapture typed supplementation, incorporate the nominal adverbially, promote its possessor to the licensed object role, apply intimate-versus-imitated possession constraints, or preserve the discarded active subject only as an adverbial embed under passive while enforcing agent suppression.
groups.readingJob: Show supplementation history, possessor-to-object promotion, intimate-possession constraint, imitation exception, means-analysis contrast, passive subject change, discarded active subject, agent prohibition, and examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses principal, supplement, and only a genuine means-versus-supplement or possession-type analysis. The application derives promotion, passive consequences, participants, and restrictions.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Lesson 17 referent structure and the ordinary nonactive owner; do not add participant-copy, manual agent, surface-spelling, example, or stem-list controls.

groups.title: Incorporated complements
groups.proposal: Build incorporated complements without changing matrix valence. Delete the embedded NNC subject only when typed referent identity links it to the matrix subject or object, and distinguish subject-oriented, object-considering, and object-changing complements through grammatical roles rather than English glosses.
groups.writingJob: Incorporate the complement nominal, preserve matrix valence and participants, derive complement-subject deletion from referent identity, and retain the typed subject or object complement relation through continuation.
groups.readingJob: Show complement role, coreferential deleted embed subject, matrix participant link, considering-versus-changing readings, unchanged valence, source boundaries, and examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the NNC and VNC Results and a complement relation only where matrix grammar and lexical analysis leave more than one real option. Coreference consequences are automatic.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse referent identity and typed lexical analysis; do not turn matrix examples into a route whitelist or add deletion, valence, or translation controls.

groups.title: Reduplication and nonactive continuation
groups.proposal: Let reduplication target the embed, matrix, or both when grammar leaves a real scope choice, and let any completed incorporated compound enter the ordinary passive or impersonal path according to its derived valence. A single-object incorporated-object Result is intransitive and therefore permits only impersonal continuation, not passive.
groups.writingJob: Apply selected reduplication scope to the correct typed Source boundary, derive its repetition, distribution, or similarity contribution, recapture the completed compound for ordinary nonactive formation, and enforce voice availability from current valence.
groups.readingJob: Show reduplication target and scope, embed and matrix boundaries, semantic contribution, current valence, passive or impersonal continuation, single-object incorporation restriction, participants, and examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses a genuine reduplication target or semantic scope and selects an available voice. The application derives form, current valence, voice availability, participant changes, and continuation.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Source-boundary reduplication and the shared nonactive owner; do not add example templates, manual voice eligibility, participant-copy, or separate Lesson 30 voice machinery.

groups.title: The nominal embed is not an agent or subject
groups.proposal: Enforce the central reading constraint across every Lesson 30 route: the incorporated nominal embed is neither finite subject nor passive agent. Preserve the finite subject pronoun as subject or actor, prohibit passive-agent expression, and derive structure from typed Source rather than English translation.
groups.writingJob: Keep nominal embed, finite subject, nuclear objects, and passive-agent restrictions distinct in every Result, including impersonals with a faceless third-singular subject, and reject analyses licensed only by an English gloss.
groups.readingJob: Show non-agent and non-subject embed status, finite subject identity, passive agent prohibition, instrument possibility, impersonal subject structure, translation warning, and examples.
groups.decisionSplit: These are automatic grammatical constraints and reading cues. No user control may reclassify the embed as subject or agent or let a translation override Source structure.
groups.controlPolicy: Add no subject, agent, or translation controls; reuse typed participant roles and nonactive authority.
